The rest of you wander wherever you please; we'll be circling the close-planted hillsides where the well-staked vines grow green. There we will see the vintner’s passion laboring every hour, daily, at his never-certain goal. With hoe, with spade, heaping, pruning, binding, he prays to all the gods, but to the sun god most of all. Soft-living 巴克科斯, caring little about his faithful servant’s dedication, rests or lolls in caves or arbors, having his way with the youngest faun. All he needs for his half-drunken reveries is stored around him in skins and flagons, jars and vessels, right and left of him, forever on hand, forever preserved, in cool, shady grottoes for all eternity. But when all the gods together, and 赫利俄斯 sun god over all the rest, have aired and moistened, warmed and roasted, and piled the cornucopia high, then, where one sole vintner labored, there comes a rustling and bustling about, in every arbor, from vine to vine. Baskets creak, buckets clatter, shoulder hampers groan with their loads, all on their way to the mighty vat, on to the wine pressers’ lusty dance. And so the sacred flesh of berries is rudely crushed, foaming, splashing, trampled to a repulsive mess.

其余的人则随心所欲地到处闲逛；我们将绕着密植的山坡转一圈，那里的藤蔓长得很茂盛。在那里，我们将看到酿酒师的热情每小时、每天都在为他永远不确定的目标而努力。他用锄头、铁锹、堆放、修剪、捆绑，向诸神祈祷，但最重要的是向太阳神祈祷。生活安逸的巴克科斯很少关心他忠实仆人的奉献，他在山洞或凉亭里休息或懒洋洋地躺着，与最小的农牧神相处。他半醉沉思所需的一切都储存在他周围的兽皮、酒壶、罐子和器皿中，左右两侧，永远在手边，永远保存在凉爽、阴凉的洞穴里，直到永远。但是，当所有的神祇一起，赫利俄斯太阳神凌驾于其他诸神之上，已经通风、湿润、温暖和烘烤，并将聚宝盆堆得高高的时候，那么，在一个唯一的酿酒师辛勤劳作的地方，每一个凉亭里，从一棵葡萄树到另一棵葡萄树，都会传来一阵沙沙声和忙碌声。篮子吱吱作响，水桶叮当作响，肩上的​​篮子装载着货物发出呻吟声，所有这些都在前往巨大的大桶的途中，在压酒师的激烈舞蹈中。就这样，浆果的神圣果肉被粗鲁地压碎、起泡、飞溅、践踏成一团令人厌恶的烂摊子。
